Clearly you do not understand how the current tax system works. You make it sound as those tax percentages relate to each other, when they do not.

When a person is included in the top bracket of 39.6% that DOES NOT mean they are pay 39.6% of their income. Rather they pay 39.6% on every dollar over $250,000. So a single individual making $250,001, will pay the top back rate of 39.6% of $1 which means he pays $0.39 in taxes on that dollar. The other $250,000 dollars are taxed at the rate for their respective brackets, the first $22,100 is taxed at 15%, every dollar from $22,101-$53,500 is taxed at the next bracket 28%, every dollar from $53,501 and $115,000 is taxed at 31%, and every dollar from $115,001 and $250,000 is taxed at 36%.

The systems lack of brackets above $250,000 and the narrow scope of each bracket result in the middle class to pay more in taxes then the upper class and the super wealthy. For example, our hypothetical individual in the above paragraph earning $250,001 would pay the same effective tax rate as an individual making $2,000,000, $10,000,000, or $50,000,000.

When a liberal like Bernie Sanders states that the rich people should be paying more. He is arguing that a single individual making $50,000,000 should have a higher effective tax rate than an individual earning $250,001. Which in my opinion seems like a fair thing to ask. The easiest way to achieve this result would be to add brackets and widen each bracket, which would then allow you to decrease the effective rate on the middle class.
